[PATH:empirical] Meta-analysis of minimum wage enforcement effects on local labor markets (e.g., studies using variation in state-level enforcement intensity in the U.S.) — Provides direct evidence on how weak vs. strong enforcement moderates the wage impact of low-skilled immigration, testing the conditional effect stated in the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Quasi-experimental studies using spatial variation in immigration shocks (e.g., the Mariel Boatlift or refugee resettlement) interacted with local minimum wage enforcement indices — Allows causal identification of the conditional wage effect by comparing labor markets with differing enforcement levels before and after immigration inflows.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical labor market models with monopsony power and minimum wage non-compliance (e.g., search-and-matching models with heterogeneous enforcement) — Formalizes the mechanism linking enforcement weakness to wage reductions, clarifying scope conditions and providing testable predictions for empirical work.

scope.domain: short-term, local labor markets with high substitutability and weak minimum wage enforcement

[PATH:empirical] Borjas (2003) 'The Labor Demand Curve Is Downward Sloping: Reexamining the Impact of Immigration on the Labor Market' — This seminal paper provides a framework for estimating the wage effects of immigration on native workers, including high-skilled immigrants, using cross-metropolitan area data over time. It can help test whether increased competition from high-skilled immigrants reduces native wages in major U.S. metropolitan areas over a 10-year period.

[PATH:empirical] Peri, G. (2012) 'The Effect of Immigration on Productivity: Evidence from U.S. States' — This study examines how high-skilled immigration affects productivity and wages in dynamic metropolitan economies, finding potential complementarities rather than pure competition. It offers a counterpoint to the displacement hypothesis and can help assess whether wage decreases occur in the long term.

[PATH:literature] Kerr, S. P., & Kerr, W. R. (2011) 'Economic Impacts of Immigration: A Survey' — This comprehensive survey synthesizes evidence on high-skilled immigration's effects on native wages, including both displacement and positive spillover channels. It can clarify the disputed status by highlighting conditions under which wage decreases or increases are observed in metropolitan labor markets.
